body: Monday, February 02 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-02 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: Growth is not the problem: third-quarter GDP rose 4.4%, the fastest in two years AP News [Jan 22], and the Fed held rates while upgrading its view of the economy CNBC [Jan 28]. Inflation is: producer prices posted their biggest gain in five months as firms passed on tariffs Reuters [Jan 30]. Households feel worse than the data, with confidence at its lowest since 2014 Bloomberg.com [Jan 27] — a K-shaped economy that keeps the Fed on hold rather than easing.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.52% and the 10Y at 4.26%, a 74 bps 10Y−2Y spread; over 20 observations the 2Y rose 5 bps and the 10Y 8 bps, a bear steepening (both up, 10Y up more) that leaves the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30). The S&P 500 closed at 6,939.03, up 1.37% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 17.44 and the DXY up 0.74% in the prior session to 96.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

New / Most Important: The Fed-chair pick was read as hawkish — traders see Kevin Warsh as the tougher choice Bloomberg.com [Jan 30] — and the reaction was violent: gold fell 10.78% and silver 31.35% in the prior session while the dollar index rose 0.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Confirmation is not a formality, since Senator Tillis will oppose the nominee until the Powell probe is resolved CNBC [Jan 30].

Playbook ✓: Stay long US equities but short duration: own the bear-steepening winners (energy, industrial capex, large banks), underweight TLT, and hedge the hawkish-chair tail with VIX calls while the VIX sits at 17.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Flip toward duration only if the jobs data Reuters flags alongside a heavy earnings week Reuters [Feb 01] disappoint, or if Warsh signals near-term cuts.

Macro Stance: Bullish. The euro-zone economy unexpectedly grew 0.3% in the fourth quarter Financial Times [Jan 30], and a Bloomberg poll has the ECB locked on hold as calls for hikes fade Bloomberg.com [Jan 30] — neutral policy while growth surprises upward. The STOXX 600 rose 3.07% over 20 sessions versus 1.37% for the S&P 500, with the Euro Stoxx 50 at 5,947.81 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Activity & Inflation: Germany is the weak link: unemployment hit a 12-year high and Merz now calls the economy his main focus Reuters [Jan 30]. The DAX was flat over 20 sessions and the CAC 40 fell 0.84%, against a 3.07% gain for the STOXX 600 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — banks and the periphery are doing the work, not the core exporters.

New / Most Important: The euro's rally to $1.20 is now the ECB's headache Bloomberg.com [Jan 28]: a stronger currency imports disinflation and squeezes exporters, so the next policy debate is about cutting, not hiking. EUR/USD closed at 1.1966, up 1.83% over 20 sessions, and GBP/USD at 1.3806 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Playbook ✓: Own domestic euro-area cyclicals and banks and underweight euro-earning exporters (autos, luxury) while EUR/USD holds near 1.1966 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Switch toward Bunds if January inflation undershoots and ECB officials start citing the euro's strength as a reason to cut.

Macro Stance: Mixed. Fourth-quarter growth slowed to 4.5%, the weakest in nearly three years, as consumption missed forecasts CNBC [Jan 18]. Beijing's response is targeted rather than broad — property-rule relief, insurer recapitalisation, a stronger-yuan agenda — which supports equity sentiment more than it fixes household demand.

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 in January Reuters [Jan 30], back below the 50 line. The feed carries no fresh non-manufacturing or industrial-output print beyond that, so the read is simple: factories are not yet feeling the policy shift. A turn needs the PMI back above 50 and new orders lifting after the Lunar New Year.

Credit Impulse: The feed carries no fresh January credit print; the latest, from mid-January, showed new loans shrinking to the least since 2018 as demand weakened Bloomberg.com [Jan 15]. Policy is working on plumbing rather than volume — Beijing plans $29 billion of special bonds to recapitalise insurers Reuters [Jan 30]. A rebound in January new loans and social financing would be the first sign that the impulse is turning.

Property: Beijing reportedly dropped the rules that sparked the property crisis, and developer shares surged Reuters [Jan 28]. The damage is still surfacing: Vanke warned its 2025 loss may have widened to $11.8 billion Bloomberg.com [Jan 30]. Relief on leverage rules helps surviving developers fund themselves, not end demand — the test is whether sales and prices stabilise in the spring selling season.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: China logged its first fiscal revenue drop since 2020 on the property slump and weak consumption Reuters [Jan 30] — the budget is constraining, not cushioning. The external front is about the currency: Xi called for the renminbi to attain global reserve-currency status Financial Times [Feb 01], a goal that implies tolerating a stronger yuan and more open capital markets. That is a currency story for portfolio flows, not a fiscal impulse for households.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 27,387.11, down 2.08% in the prior session but up 3.98% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite ended at 4,117.95, up 3.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). ASHR rose 1.8% and KWEB 3.91% over 20 sessions, while USD/CNY fell 0.69% to 6.9480 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); the yuan hit a 32-month high earlier in the week as the PBOC strengthened its guidance Reuters [Jan 27].

New / Most Important: The signal is the policy mix, not the data: leverage rules for developers eased Reuters [Jan 28], insurers are being recapitalised Reuters [Jan 30] and the yuan is being guided higher. That favours financials and Hong Kong-listed platforms over exporters, while the weak PMI keeps pressure on Beijing to add direct demand support.

Playbook ✓: Own China through Hong Kong financials and internet (FXI, KWEB) on dips, treat developer rallies as trades until Vanke's restructuring settles, and avoid exporters exposed to a firmer yuan. Upgrade to Bullish if January credit data rebound and the PMI returns above 50; cut if USD/CNY reverses its 0.69% 20-session decline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). ⚠ Divergence: Xi wants a strong, reserve-grade currency Financial Times [Feb 01] and the yuan hit a 32-month high days ago Reuters [Jan 27], yet the PMI is in contraction at 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30] — currency strength is tightening conditions just as domestic demand needs relief.

Macro Stance: Bullish. Polls show Takaichi's party poised for a landslide Reuters [Feb 01] in the Feb. 8 Lower House vote The Japan Times [Jan 27], and the BOJ's January summary shows members debating the risk of falling behind the curve on inflation Reuters [Feb 01]. A strong mandate plus a central bank leaning toward normalisation is good for domestic earnings and for banks.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 153.16, down 2.28% over 20 sessions and 3.37% over five as the yen rallied, while the Nikkei 225 ended at 53,322.85, up 5.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Equities absorbed a stronger yen, which says the rally is domestic and financial rather than export-led.

Playbook ✓: Own domestic financials and reflation plays into the vote and hedge exporters' yen exposure. Cut the call if the LDP misses a majority, or if a consumption-tax suspension, which the finance minister says Tokyo is carefully considering Reuters [Jan 29], reignites a selloff in long-dated JGBs.

Macro Stance: Bearish for domestic equities. Inflation jumped to 3.8% The Guardian [Jan 27], CBA economists expect the cash rate to rise to 3.85% CommBank [Jan 28], and the hike is expected at Tuesday's meeting ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Jan 29]. A central bank tightening against the global trend raises the discount rate for the whole market.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7047, up 5.53% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 ended at 8,869.10, up only 1.78% and down 1.08% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A currency outrunning the index is an earnings headwind for offshore earners and a funding-cost squeeze for mortgaged households.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive ASX sectors and AUD-earning exporters, keep long AUD/USD through the decision, and prefer bank margins to housing-linked names. Reverse if the RBA holds instead of moving to 3.85% CommBank [Jan 28] — that would push AUD back toward 0.6678, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Monetary & Activity: GDP grew 3.6% in 2025, according to GUS data reported by Rzeczpospolita Rzeczpospolita [Jan 30], and MPC member Kotecki said a rate cut could come as early as February Bloomberg.com [Jan 16] — easing into strong growth, the best mix for domestic equities. With the zloty firm, imported inflation is not the constraint on the council.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5139, down 1.98% over 20 sessions, with EUR/PLN at 4.2041; EPOL rose 6.82% and the WIG20TR ETF 5.69% over 20 sessions, led by PGE (+14.04%), Orlen (+12.33%) and PKO BP (+8.71%), while KGHM fell 10.7% and CD Projekt 8.0% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The WIG20 hit its highest level in 18 years Business Insider Polska [Jan 29]; CD Projekt's drop came on the day videogame stocks slid on Google's AI world-builder Reuters [Jan 30].

Companies: KGHM's CEO was dismissed and a successor named in what Business Insider Polska called an earthquake Business Insider Polska [Jan 30], just as silver and copper reversed. LPP will pay a record dividend of at least 800 zł per share Rzeczpospolita [Jan 30], and PKO BP and PZU, up 8.71% and 5.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), remain the income core of the index.

Security & New Development: Poland signed off on a €3.5 billion 'breakthrough' anti-drone defence system TVP World [Jan 30], the clearest sign that defence spending is now a domestic investment theme. Combined with a possible February cut Bloomberg.com [Jan 16], fiscal and monetary policy are both leaning pro-growth.

Playbook ✓: Own PKO BP and PGE and keep zloty exposure unhedged while EUR/PLN holds near 4.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); trim KGHM until governance settles. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 sits at an 18-year high Business Insider Polska [Jan 29] while KGHM lost its CEO Business Insider Polska [Jan 30] and fell 10.7% in a day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — political risk at state champions has not been priced out.

Narrative: Consensus still treats tech as one AI trade, but the tape split it: XLK was flat over 20 sessions (-0.06%) while MSFT fell 11.03%, ORCL 15.56% and PLTR 17.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The market is separating owners of scarce AI capacity from seat-based software it fears AI will disrupt.

Reported: Microsoft lost $357 billion of market value as the stock plunged the most since 2020 CNBC [Jan 29], with slowing cloud growth set against huge AI spending Business Insider [Jan 29]. IBM, by contrast, jumped 8% on its beat CNBC [Jan 28], and AAPL gained 4.61% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Palantir reports on Feb. 2 The Motley Fool [Jan 27] after a 17.53% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), so the bar has been lowered for an AI-revenue name. In hardware, the memory squeeze that lifts suppliers is a cost for device makers — upside sits with storage and memory vendors, not assemblers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: IBM's 8% jump CNBC [Jan 28] shows the 'AI eats software' trade is too blunt: a legacy vendor was rewarded because AI is lifting its software demand. If AI attach shows up in renewals, the most-hated SaaS names become the cheapest AI beneficiaries.

Narrative: Communication services is where AI spending is already being paid for: XLC rose 2.0% and META 8.55% over 20 sessions while XLK went nowhere and NFLX fell 10.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Platforms with ad engines can fund capex from revenue, which is exactly what investors now demand.

Reported: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger-than-expected revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28], proof that a big AI budget is forgiven when the top line accelerates with it. META gave back 2.95% in the prior session as the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet headlines the busiest week of the reporting period alongside Amazon CNBC [Feb 01]. GOOGL rose 7.99% over 20 sessions to 338.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); a cloud acceleration that matches Meta's revenue story would carry the whole sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Google's AI is destroying value inside its own sector: videogame stocks slid on its model that turns prompts into playable worlds Reuters [Jan 30]. XLC is a bet on the AI platforms, not on content owners — underweight gaming and streaming.

Narrative: Financials lagged — XLF fell 2.43% and JPM 5.07% over 20 sessions while GS rose 6.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The driver that matters now is the Fed pick: Warsh is likely to boost Wall Street rule easing Reuters [Jan 30], and a bear-steepening curve widens lending margins.

Reported: Visa beat first-quarter estimates as holiday sales boosted payment volumes Reuters [Jan 29] — card-network spending is intact. BAC rose 2.86% and JPM 2.74% over five sessions as the banks stabilised (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Capital-markets franchises: US high-grade bond sales topped $200 billion in a record yearly start Bloomberg.com [Jan 29], feeding underwriting fees at GS and the money-centre banks. Deregulation under a new chair is an estimate driver not yet in consensus numbers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits next to the banks: Bloomberg warns private credit is headed for a software shock Bloomberg.com [Feb 01] — the same AI-disruption fear that crushed software stocks now threatens loans to software companies. Own the money-centre banks, avoid BDCs concentrated in software lending.

Narrative: Energy is the clearest trend of the year: XLE rose 14.18% over 20 sessions as Brent climbed 16.17% to 70.69 and WTI 13.57% to 65.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Iran is the driver — oil surged to a five-month high on worries the US could attack Reuters [Jan 29].

Reported: Exxon beat as Permian and Guyana fields took output to a 40-year high Reuters [Jan 30]; XOM rose 17.5% and CVX 16.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Volume growth, not price, carried the majors' quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: Gas-weighted producers: Henry Hub is still up 18.12% over 20 sessions despite a 17.46% five-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), so first-quarter realised prices should beat estimates set before the cold snap. Producers combining record volumes with higher spot prices carry the cleanest upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The premium is fragile: Brent's 20-session gain rests on an Iran attack that has not happened Reuters [Jan 29], and the gas market shows how fast a premium unwinds — Henry Hub lost 17.46% in five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Hold producers with volume growth, not crude itself.

Narrative: Industrials have become an AI-power trade: XLI rose 6.65% and CAT 14.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), and NERC forecasts peak demand rising 24% on new data-centre loads Utility Dive [Jan 30]. Turbines, gensets and grid gear are the bottleneck, which gives their makers pricing power that a soft factory cycle cannot erode.

Reported: Caterpillar jumped as power-generation demand made it a surprise AI play Barron's [Jan 29], and GE Vernova's fourth-quarter gas-turbine orders surged 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30]. GE rose 2.65% in the prior session while BA fell 7.31% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Power-generation suppliers: a 74% jump in turbine orders Utility Dive [Jan 30] converts into revenue over several years, so backlog-driven upside persists even if the AI capex debate cools. Defence primes with European order books are the second leg.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cycle under the rally is weak: the December ISM manufacturing PMI was 47.9% PR Newswire [Jan 05]. XLI is pricing capex, not a cyclical recovery — own power and defence, not short-cycle machinery that needs a manufacturing upturn.

Narrative: Discretionary is K-shaped: XLY rose 1.47% over 20 sessions while TSLA fell 4.29%, NKE 2.98% and HD rose 8.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Confidence at its lowest since 2014 Bloomberg.com [Jan 27] has not yet shown up in housing-linked names.

Reported: GM hit an all-time high on upbeat results and a buyback, with its CFO calling the stock undervalued Yahoo Finance [Jan 27] — trucks and capital returns beat EV ambition. TSLA rose 3.32% in the prior session but is down 4.15% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon reports in the busiest week of the season CNBC [Feb 01]; AMZN is up 3.67% over 20 sessions at 239.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). AWS acceleration plus retail margin discipline is the set-up for a beat, and a modest 20-session gain leaves room for a positive reaction.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Sentiment and spending have decoupled: confidence sits at a 2014 low Bloomberg.com [Jan 27] while the S&P 500 is 1.37% higher over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The sector's bigger risk is a hawkish Fed and higher real rates, not the shopper.

Narrative: Staples are the hiding place: XLP rose 7.51% over 20 sessions and 1.68% in the prior session, with WMT up 6.94% and COST 9.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A hawkish Fed pick and crowded tech positioning keep the rotation into defensives alive.

Reported: Procter & Gamble missed revenue estimates on slower US growth Reuters [Jan 22] — the sector rally is not about volumes. The winners are price-makers with traffic, Walmart and Costco, not the branded-goods makers.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco: membership and grocery traffic hold up in a K-shaped economy, and both have outpaced the S&P 500's 1.37% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Upside comes from mix — services and membership fees — not from price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: P&G's miss Reuters [Jan 22] says US demand for branded staples is slowing even as the group re-rates. If defensives are bid only for safety, a risk-on turn after strong Big Tech prints would hit XLP first.

Narrative: Healthcare is the policy loser: XLV was flat over 20 sessions (-0.04%) while UNH fell 19.46% over five sessions and LLY 3.49% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Medicare rates and drug-price politics are compressing the multiples of the sector's biggest names.

Reported: UnitedHealth forecast its first revenue drop in nearly four decades and the shares plunged Reuters [Jan 27]; managed care now trades like a regulated utility with negative growth. UNH closed at 286.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity drugs: Lilly's CEO says Medicare coverage could change the game for the pill launch CNBC [Jan 30], and Lilly is among the week's reporters CNBC [Jan 30]. Volume from new coverage is the one clear estimate upside in the sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lilly is a policy winner in a policy-loser sector CNBC [Jan 30]: Medicare coverage expands the market even as negotiation squeezes legacy drugs. Pair long LLY against managed care until UNH proves a revenue floor.

Narrative: Materials were January's winner and are now the unwind: XLB is still up 8.64% over 20 sessions, but gold fell 10.78%, silver 31.35% and copper 4.51% in the prior session, with NEM down 11.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The Warsh pick punctured the debasement trade.

Reported: Dow will cut 4,500 jobs and forecast weak revenue amid sluggish demand Reuters [Jan 29] — chemicals have no AI tailwind. FCX fell 7.52% in the prior session but remains up 18.59% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers: copper soared past $14,500 a ton Bloomberg.com [Jan 29] before the retreat, and the front month at 5.90 is still up 4.74% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Quarterly realised prices should run ahead of estimates set before the spike.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper fell far less than gold and silver in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30): the AI data-centre and grid metal is decoupling from the precious-metals unwind. After a run past $14,500 Bloomberg.com [Jan 29], own FCX over gold miners.

Narrative: REITs are fighting the curve: XLRE rose 2.68% over 20 sessions while the 10Y rose 8 bps to 4.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30; US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30). A hawkish Fed chair pick limits the rate relief the sector needs.

Reported: Keppel DC REIT's second-half DPU rose 7.1% on acquisitions and strong portfolio reversion The Business Times [Jan 30] — data-centre landlords are delivering where office and housing-linked REITs are not. XLRE itself closed at 41.43, up 0.15% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre landlords: the Keppel result The Business Times [Jan 30] shows rent reversion running with AI demand, and NERC's 24% peak-demand forecast Utility Dive [Jan 30] says the scarce asset is powered land. Prefer data-centre and tower REITs within XLRE.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Bear steepening is the enemy, but the 2Y fell 8 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30): if weak jobs data pull the front end lower, rate-sensitive REITs are the first to squeeze.

Narrative: Utilities have the demand but not the politics: XLU rose 1.31% over 20 sessions while CEG fell 20.55% and NEE rose 9.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). NERC forecasts peak demand up 24% on data-centre loads Utility Dive [Jan 30].

Reported: The read-across came from suppliers: GE Vernova's gas-turbine orders surged 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30], so new generation is booked years out and incumbents with existing plants hold the scarce asset. The market is not yet paying merchant nuclear for that scarcity: CEG fell 2.36% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with contracted data-centre load: NEE's 9.49% gain against a 1.85% drop for merchant generator VST over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) shows the market paying for rate-base growth over power-price exposure that politics may cap.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Utilities want $31 billion more from customers Business Insider [Jan 31] — affordability, not demand, is now the binding constraint. Prefer regulated wires over merchant power.

Narrative: European autos are losing on three fronts: Chinese brands now make one in 10 cars sold in Europe Bloomberg.com [Jan 30], the euro's run toward $1.20 Bloomberg.com [Jan 28] hurts exporters, and price wars squeeze margins. The SXAP tracker fell 6.24% over 20 sessions, BMW 9.24%, Mercedes 6.68% and Renault 12.32% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Reported: The read-across from Detroit was positive — GM hit an all-time high on results and a buyback Yahoo Finance [Jan 27] — but it came from US trucks and capital returns that European makers cannot copy. VW's US ADR fell 2.42% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Stellantis is the cheapest restructuring option: STLA rose 1.33% over five sessions despite a 9.37% 20-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). With no fresh catalyst in the feed, upside depends on a European volume recovery.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Volkswagen held up best — VOW3 is down only 3.57% over 20 sessions versus 9.24% for BMW (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A mass-market maker is outlasting premium brands, the opposite of the usual quality preference in a downturn.

Narrative: Semis remain the AI hardware core: SOXX rose 14.99% over 20 sessions, with ASML up 33.01%, MU 45.36% and INTC 25.93%, despite a 4.11% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Memory is the binding constraint — Samsung and SK Hynix warn the crunch will last until 2027 Nikkei Asia [Jan 29].

Reported: ASML's record orders smashed estimates as AI spurs demand Bloomberg.com [Jan 28], while AMD fell on MI450-series delay rumours Yahoo Finance Australia [Jan 30] and lost 6.13% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and lithography: a shortage expected to last until 2027 Nikkei Asia [Jan 29] lets contract prices reset higher, and ASML's record orders Bloomberg.com [Jan 28] lock in equipment revenue. MU and ASML carry the cleanest estimate upside, with TSM, up 8.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), next.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia is the laggard inside the boom, up only 2.48% over 20 sessions while AVGO fell 4.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The money is flowing to scarcity — memory and lithography — not to the GPU and custom-chip leaders.

Rewarded: Companies showing AI spending already paying back, or selling scarce capacity: Meta jumped on its revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28], IBM on its beat CNBC [Jan 28], Caterpillar on power-generation demand Barron's [Jan 29], and ASML on record orders Bloomberg.com [Jan 28]. GM's all-time high on results and a buyback Yahoo Finance [Jan 27] shows old-economy names with capital returns get paid too.

Punished: Capex without visible payback and anything AI could disrupt: Microsoft lost $357 billion of market value CNBC [Jan 29], and PLTR, ORCL and MSFT fell 17.53%, 15.56% and 11.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Weak guidance was not forgiven — UnitedHealth plunged on its first revenue-drop forecast in nearly four decades Reuters [Jan 27] — and P&G's revenue miss Reuters [Jan 22] mattered even in a hot staples tape.

Pattern: The bar is relative. Meta was rewarded because a stronger revenue forecast came with its spending CNBC [Jan 28], while Microsoft's mix of slowing cloud growth and huge AI spending produced its steepest drop in nearly six years Business Insider [Jan 29]. Physical bottlenecks — memory, turbines, power gear — earn a premium, seat-based software a discount, and beats in stocks that ran hardest into the print get sold.

Attention into EPS: The busiest stretch of the season tests the same question: Palantir on Feb. 2 The Motley Fool [Jan 27], then Alphabet and Amazon CNBC [Feb 01], and Lilly alongside the jobs data CNBC [Jan 30]. Alphabet must pair capex with cloud acceleration, Amazon needs AWS to justify its spending, and Palantir must prove it is not priced like SaaS; Reuters frames the week as a test for stocks after Microsoft's swoon Reuters [Feb 01].

Playbook: Buy beat-and-raise names on first-day weakness only when revenue guidance rose; fade beats where the stock ran into the print and where capex rises without revenue guidance. Pair long memory and lithography scarcity (MU, ASML) against seat-based software until renewals show AI attach, and stop the pair if MSFT reclaims 483.62, its close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Attention Gap: Global attention is on AI and the metals crash, but Beijing quietly shifted: it reportedly dropped the rules that sparked the property crisis Reuters [Jan 28] and plans $29 billion of special bonds to recapitalise insurers Reuters [Jan 30]. FXI fell 2.87% in the prior session while staying up 3.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — investors still trade China as a tech story, not as a balance-sheet repair story.

Exposure & Risk: Express it through FXI (39.61) and ASHR (33.44) rather than single developers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), adding Hong Kong-listed insurers as the direct policy beneficiaries. The risk is credit: Vanke warned its 2025 loss may have widened to $11.8 billion Bloomberg.com [Jan 30]. Exit if official January home-price data show the decline accelerating.

Attention Gap: The yen and the election take the headlines, but the BOJ's January summary shows members debating the risk of being behind the curve on inflation Reuters [Feb 01]. With USD/JPY at 153.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), a BOJ that worries about falling behind has room to keep hiking, and the direct beneficiary is bank net interest income.

Exposure & Risk: Express via MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho ADRs, funded from yen-sensitive exporters given USD/JPY's 2.28% fall over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Risks: a hung election or a consumption-tax suspension Reuters [Jan 29] that triggers a disorderly JGB selloff, and a BOJ that pauses if the yen keeps strengthening.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 76,974.45, down 2.09% on the day, 13.61% over five sessions and 15.59% over 20; ether closed at 2,267.96, down 24.96% over five sessions, and solana at 100.85, down 27.52% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-01). IBIT fell 6.33% and COIN 10.24% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The FT says bitcoin slid to its lowest level since the 2025 tariff shock Financial Times [Feb 01].

New / Most Important: The selloff is macro: Warsh is read as hawkish Bloomberg.com [Jan 30], which hits the most liquidity-sensitive risk first, and liquidations topped $2.5 billion as bitcoin, ether and XRP plunged Decrypt [Jan 31]. Traders are betting billions on a drop below $75,000 and bailing on upside CoinDesk [Feb 01]. MSTR still rose 4.55% in the prior session to 149.71 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), a sign retail treats the treasury companies as dip vehicles.

Playbook: Stay underweight. If $75,000 breaks CoinDesk [Feb 01], expect forced selling around leveraged treasury companies — do not use MSTR as a dip vehicle. Re-enter via IBIT, at 47.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), only after bitcoin holds above its prior completed daily close of 76,974.45 for a week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-01) and dollar strength fades.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY rose 0.74% to 96.99 in the prior session but is down 1.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); the bounce came as traders priced a more hawkish Fed chair Bloomberg.com [Jan 30]. The curve is bear-steepening — the 10Y is up 8 bps over 20 observations to 4.26% and the 30Y sits at 4.87% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30) — while TLT is flat over 20 sessions at 87.13 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Credit Check: Credit is open and calm: HYG rose 0.61% and LQD 0.34% over 20 sessions to 81.12 and 110.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), and US high-grade bond sales topped $200 billion in a record yearly start Bloomberg.com [Jan 29]. The crack is in private credit, which Bloomberg says is headed for a software shock Bloomberg.com [Feb 01].

Portfolio Implication: Liquidity supports equities, but a hawkish chair and the biggest producer-price gain in five months Reuters [Jan 30] argue against duration. Hold front-end IG, underweight TLT, and keep a long-dollar sleeve against gold until the Warsh confirmation path clears. Watch AI-capex debt supply: heavier issuance, not defaults, is what would widen spreads.

What Is Priced: Markets priced a hawk in one session: traders see Warsh as the more hawkish pick Bloomberg.com [Jan 30], gold and silver fell 10.78% and 31.35%, and the DXY rose 0.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Yet over five observations the 2Y still fell 8 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30) — the repricing hit the long end and real assets, not near-term policy expectations.

Conditional Expression: If confirmation advances and Warsh stresses a smaller balance sheet, stay short TLT, long the dollar and sell gold rallies. If the Tillis blockade holds CNBC [Jan 30] and the nomination stalls, fade the dollar and rebuy GLD, down 10.27% to 444.95 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Risk: The one-day repricing assumes Warsh governs as a hawk; a quick dovish signal aligned with the White House would squeeze the crowded short-gold, long-dollar trade. A soft jobs print in a week Reuters already frames as a test for stocks Reuters [Feb 01] would do the same.

What Is Priced: Polls show the LDP poised for a landslide Reuters [Feb 01] in the Feb. 8 vote The Japan Times [Jan 27]; the Nikkei 225 is up 5.53% over 20 sessions while USD/JPY fell 2.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A strong mandate plus continued BOJ normalisation is in the price.

Conditional Expression: Landslide with a consumption-tax suspension Reuters [Jan 29]: own Japanese banks and domestic reflation, pay long-end JGB yields, and expect the yen to soften on fiscal worries. Hung result: buy the yen and sell exporters and the Nikkei, since a weak mandate would stall both fiscal and reform plans.

Risk: The yen is the swing factor — USD/JPY fell 3.37% in five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), and a disorderly move after the vote could bring official intervention. Polls can also miss in a winter snap election.

Instrument & Risk: SLV closed at 75.44 and is still up 17.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), so the move has not fully round-tripped.
